recipes.name: Delicious Stuffed Potato Pancakes
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Mix together potatoes, flour, baking powder, 3 eggs, salt, and pepper in a bowl. In another bowl, mix ground beef, onion, garlic salt, 1 egg, and bread crumbs until well-combined.

Heat oil in a skillet over medium-low heat; drop a rounded tablespoon of potato mixture into the hot skillet. Spread and flatten pancake out a little, and place about 2 teaspoons of beef mixture on top, spreading filling out almost to the edges of pancake. Drop another rounded tablespoon of potato mixture on top, and spread it out to completely cover beef. Fry until the bottom of pancake is golden brown, about 5 minutes; flip and fry other side until golden, 1 to 2 more minutes. Transfer pancake to a paper towel-lined plate. Repeat with remaining potato mixture and beef filling.

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Stuffed Potato Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Potato pancakes are stuffed with seasoned ground beef and pan-fried until golden brown. Perfect for that meat-and-potatoes eater in your house.

review.reviewBody: these were really good. But I was not sure if the meat should be cooked before adding, so I cooked the meat before adding the egg and bread crumbs to be on the safe side. My kids liked them esp since they could eat them with their hands. I was a little impatient waiting to flip them becasue I was in a hurry, so I put them in the oven until I was done cooking them all to make sure they cooked thru. I will be making these again. I think I will try usung sausage and them freezing them. They would be great to reheat for a quick breakfast on the go.

This was a super delicious recipe and I will be making this again. It is important to note that I changed a few things up. I increased the potato and meat portions. After I grated my potato, I pressed the water out with a ricer. This helped keep my pancakes together when it was time to fry. I precooked my ground beef making sure to drain and rinse excess fat. There were some extra seasonings added to the beef afterwards including Worcestershire sauce, extra garlic powder, and ketchup. I also added garlic powder and Italian seasoning to my potato mixture. 
This was completely amazing and it could work well with different toppings. My husband enjoyed them with ketchup. I used sour cream, cilantro, and salsa. It was very good.

I made this recipe several times and my family loves it! I do take a short cut and use a box of dry potato pancake mix instead of making the pancakes from scratch. There is no need to precook the meat as it cooks along with the pancake mix. Use a non-stick pan and they will not stick. I serve this as a dinner meal topped with brown gravy and soup and vegs with it.

This recipe was very delicious! I basically had to pulse the potatoes in a blender after cutting them into tiny pieces so it could heat up on the stove. I added just a bit of creole seasoning to the potatoes and I added some fresh spinach to the beef. These came out delicious and my family absolutely loves them! Only thing is it took me two hours to peel, cut and blend the potatoes and get everything ready. The cheese is an amazing addition, especially when biting into the potato pancake. 8.5/10 would make again.

U made this just this morning for the ranch crew and it was a huge success! I cooked only half of the amount the reciped makes in the beginning because I was unsure how they would go over...they were gone before I could start the second half =) I had a bit of trouble getting the potato mix to cook fully though. Next time I think I will brown them and put them on a sheet pan in the oven, just to be sure. I also took the suggestion of cooking the meat prior to assembling the pancakes which was a good idea as everything came together very well. Next time I will prepare and cook the sausage the night before as well as prep the potato mix because it took me considerably longer than 20 minutes to prepare (nearly an hour due to the potato grating) All in all, this recipe was as delicious as it looks and I will be adding it to the breakfast menu for sure!

Made this for dinner tonight, and it was delicious and filling! I cooked the beef and drained the fat before filling the pancakes. For the beef, I added spices (garlic and a little allspice). To the potatoe mixture, I used a whole onion and 3 cloves of garlic for taste, and also, added 1/2 cup of additional flour and 1/4 cup of milk (which makes the potatoe more of a batter, which is easier to spread when cooking.
Used shredded fresh potatoes (in a green bag)found in Dairy dept at Kroger and that made it much easier! Added Garlic and I pre-cooked meat mixture to eliminate grease. These were awesome!

I thought this recipe looked neat, so I wanted to try it. There was no way I was going to peel and grate 8 potatoes for a recipe I had never even eaten. So, I used 2-20oz bags of simply potatoes shredded plain hashed browns. I also just minced instead of grated the onion. I found making the patties to be fairly easy and used kitchen scoops to get the correct amounts. The patties did stay together well, but I feared they burger wouldn't cook in time, and cooked them much longer than suggested. Overall they didn't have a lot of flavor though, and the burger couldn't be tasted much. I ended up eating it with ketchup and it tasted more like french fries with a little burger then. I made 5 so far, but will probably just cook the rest in a pan separately.

I made a few changes and will rate the result of those changes. Firstly, this is a great mealtime idea; only my meal was breakfast! Secondly, I will, because of the response, do this again. I had enough egg substitute to use in the potato mixture and only one egg left in the fridge which I used for the "filling". My filling was a good premium breakfast sausage! I omitted the garlic (no big fan, here) and used maybe a couple tablespoons finely diced onion. I pre-cooked the sausage and onion so the onion wouldn't be crunchy, just until the pink was gone in the meat, drained it really well and then continued with recipe as written. I put a drizzle of maple syrup on mine and the GK's wanted a dusting of powdered sugar on theirs. Big tall glasses of OJ, steaming coffee and a delicious breakfast was enjoyed by all!!

Yummmo! Made these last night and I had the boys (big and small) begging before I was even done cooking them all! As a time saver I used Simply Potatoes shredded hashbrown potatoes - 3 bags worth. Topped both with shredded cheese as others had suggested. Had 2 skillets going: one with ground beef middle and one w/bulk sausage middle. So breakfast AND dinner cooked at same time! **FYI**Didn't cook either beef or sausage before putting in middle and frying and came out PERFECTLY DONE**Yes, BOTH meats!! Thank you so much for a recipe that now MUST go into dinner rotation!
Made directed in my waffle iron!
These weren't out of this world, but they were pretty tasty. My hubby seemed to like them well enough too.
This was really good. I cooked the meat ahead of time.
It was good but a lot of work and mess, but fun to try,.
I am definitely trying this for Hanukkah.
I fried the burgers first and added cheese -- AWESOME

Very difficult to make!! I don't know how you are supposed to get the ground beef fully cooked by cooking it in a pan with the potatoes on the outside. I ended up putting them in the microwave after they came out of the pan in order to cook the beef. 

They tasted ok...but very time consuming for a mediocre product.
Not sure what I did wrong with this recipe, but it kept falling apart rather than sticking together. I made it as written. It was a waste for us. Won't make it again.

I found it was better to dry the shredded potatoes before combing in egg mixture. Also, make the cakes small and relatively thin so the potatoes can cook through. The kids ate them with ketchup and said them to be delicious.
